# Results registry — schema

The DDL is `src/sisteer/registry/schema.sql`, rendered from `schema_def.py`; a database is built from the migration files in `src/sisteer/registry/migrations/` (`registry init`), never from `schema.sql` directly. This page lists every table and column with its constraints and, for a nullable column, the reason it may be null; the SQL of the table constraints, views and triggers is in `schema.sql`.

Conventions: every `CHECK (col IN (...))` list comes from `vocab.py` (`vocabulary.md`); booleans are INTEGER 0/1; every `*_utc TEXT` is ISO-8601 UTC with milliseconds (`…Z`); every `*_json TEXT` is `json_valid`; hashes are lowercase hex; foreign keys are enforced (sentinel columns by trigger). Item-scale tables carry `written_utc INTEGER` (epoch ms) + `record_sha256 BLOB` as their order key and keep no history rows; their history is the record log.

Scale classes: run-scale = `paper_round`, `model`, `si_text`, `fit_search`, `fit_trial`, `eval`, `item_set`, `judge`, `instrument`, `decode_policy`, `sampling_mode_policy`, `computation`, `ruling`, `ruling_state`, `object`, `run`, `run_state_event`, `judgment`, `run_metric`, `run_contrast`, `artifact`, `item_withdrawal`, `roster_entry`, `disposition`, `snapshot`, `parity_gate`, `source_revision`, `observation`, `withdrawal`, `source_watermark`, `source_state`, `mirror_ack`, `file_arrival`; item-scale = `run_degeneration`, `item_result`, `item_flags`, `source_status`; ledgers = `schema_migration`, `record_ingest`, `record_delivery`, `record_refusal`, `record_refusal_fact`, `analysis`, `analysis_input`, `analysis_artifact`, `ordered_fact_record`, `ordered_fact_carrier`, `fold_observation`, `record_run_index`, `blocked_records`, `row_history`; staging (transient) = `revision_staging_record`, `revision_staging_file`, `record_cursor`.

Soft reference (no DB FK, documented): `eval.default_item_set_id` → `item_set.item_set_id` is circular with `item_set.eval_id` → `eval.eval_id`; enforcing both as dependency-blocking FKs would deadlock the seed.

### `item_withdrawal` (run-scale)

A producer's retraction of ONE natively emitted item_result row it filed under the wrong run (migration 0020). An `item_withdrawal` record names a run and a list of exact item keys; the fold writes one row here per key (the observation pattern) and marks the item_result row whose order key is below the record's (`withdrawn_by_record_sha256`, `withdrawn_reason`); `v_item_result_current` and every current-item predicate exclude a marked row. Rows of an adapter revision are never targeted (their membership is the revision's). The latest record naming a key (by order key) stands; a row re-filed with a greater order key than the withdrawal's stands as a new measurement.

### `source_status` (item-scale)

What ONE adapter read of ONE source found, filed under every paper source string (`lane_source_legacy`) the adapter covers — the registry-side half of the paper's status contract. Written by the adapter runner after each accepted read, once per read (the revision tag keys the row), so the history of a source's reads is the table and the head read is `v_source_status_current`. `extra_json` carries the adapter's FACTS (the producer records it read and reduced: ruled operating points, dose tables, the record's roster, engines); the paper's guards DECIDE on them in the reader, the registry only carries the evidence. `v_source_status` reduces the head reads to one row per (`lane_source_legacy`, adapter) and folds in the LATEST revision of each source, accepted or refused, so a refused re-read is visible there (`ok = 0`, `extra_json.refuse`) instead of hidden behind the accepted head it leaves current.

### `record_ingest` (ledger-scale)

Replayable FILE-scale ledger (spec: every file's sha and ingest_seq): ingest_seq is the dense rank of the file in ARRIVAL order — (arrival_utc, first_written_utc, logical sha256, uri) over the whole log — so a file the live registry folds is always head + 1 and every row above a head a reader has seen is new to it; every row of the index carries its file's rank. A rebuild reproduces the order from the file_arrival facts in the log (a file with none takes arrival_utc = first_written_utc). Per-record dedupe is the row_history event key / the item order key, not this table.

Primary key: (`file_uri`); unique: (`record_file_id`); (`ingest_seq`)

| column | type | null | check / reference | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `file_uri` | TEXT | NOT NULL |  | Root-relative LOGICAL path (no .gz). |
| `record_file_id` | INTEGER | NOT NULL |  | First 63 bits of sha256(file_uri): the arrival-independent integer id item rows point at. |
| `file_sha256` | TEXT | NOT NULL | pattern `SHA256` | sha256 of the DECOMPRESSED bytes (two files may share it; each is its own ledger row). |
| `first_written_utc` | TEXT | NOT NULL | pattern `UTC_MS` | The smallest written_utc among the file's accepted records — the tie-break after arrival_utc, and the arrival of a file the live registry never folded. |
| `arrival_utc` | TEXT | NOT NULL | pattern `UTC_MS` | THE ordering stamp: the live registry's clock at the file's FIRST fold, strictly after the head's (max(cycle clock, head + 1 ms)); kept for the file's life (a re-read or re-keyed file keeps it). A harvester-originated file (records/harvester/) and a file a replay finds no file_arrival fact for take their first_written_utc. |
| `n_records` | INTEGER | NOT NULL |  |  |
| `ingest_seq` | INTEGER | NOT NULL |  |  |

Indexes: `idx_record_ingest_sha` (file_sha256), `idx_record_ingest_order` (arrival_utc, first_written_utc, file_sha256, file_uri).

### `record_refusal_fact` (ledger-scale)

The harvester's DURABLE fact of one refusal judgment: one row per (refused record, judging stamp), written into the log as a `record_refusal` record under records/harvester/<day>/record_refusal-<sha12>.jsonl and folded here by its own apply path (INSERT OR IGNORE, no row_history), so every mirror and every rebuild reproduce every refusal ever made under every stamp, while `record_refusal` keeps only the current judgment per record. Derived from `record_refusal` at the START of every cycle (before any re-attempt can replace a row) and again at its END; a row refused before the stamp was kept is a fact under 'unverified' with extra_json.backfilled = true. Pure function of the log: a rebuild carries the same rows.

Primary key: (`record_sha256`, `judged_with`)

| column | type | null | check / reference | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `record_sha256` | TEXT | NOT NULL | pattern `SHA256` | The refused record (records.record_sha): the key `record_refusal` holds it under. |
| `record_uri` | TEXT | NOT NULL |  | The logical uri the record was refused under (`<file>#<line>` for a record inside a file). |
| `record_type` | TEXT | nullable |  | an envelope without a readable type |
| `field` | TEXT | nullable |  | an envelope-level refusal names no field |
| `reason` | TEXT | NOT NULL |  |  |
| `judged_with` | TEXT | NOT NULL | pattern `STAMP16_OR_UNVERIFIED` | The judging code's stamp (harvest.validator_stamp) the refusal was made under, or 'unverified' for a refusal recorded before the stamp was kept. |
| `refused_utc` | TEXT | NOT NULL | pattern `UTC_MS` | record_refusal.refused_utc of the judgment: when the refusal was made (never the cycle that derived the fact). |
| `producer_json` | TEXT | nullable | pattern `JSON` | the refused file could not be re-read for the record's producer block (moved, unreadable, or a line that is not JSON) |
| `cycle_utc` | TEXT | NOT NULL | pattern `UTC_MS` | The clock of the harvester cycle that derived the fact (the record id is minted over the payload WITHOUT it). |
| `extra_json` | TEXT | NOT NULL default '{}' | pattern `JSON` | `backfilled: true` for a row refused before the stamp was kept. |

Indexes: `idx_record_refusal_fact_uri` (record_uri), `idx_record_refusal_fact_cycle` (cycle_utc).

### `analysis` (ledger-scale)

An ANALYSIS filed over ingested runs and objects: a prefill-only or offline computation -- a routing capture, an ablation, an efficiency study -- with results but no run-shaped home (no eval, no generation). One row per filing, written into the log as an `analysis` record under records/analyses/<day>/ by `registry analysis file --spec` and folded by the ledger-fact apply path (INSERT OR IGNORE, no row_history): the row IS the fact, keyed by `analysis_id` = uuid5 over the analysis's identity (its name, its code sha and its inputs; `sisteer.registry.analysis.analysis_id`), so a re-filing of the same analysis is a duplicate and a changed input set or code sha is a new analysis. Its inputs are `analysis_input` rows, its files `analysis_artifact` rows.

Primary key: (`analysis_id`)

| column | type | null | check / reference | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `analysis_id` | TEXT | NOT NULL |  | uuid5 over the analysis's identity: canonical JSON of {name, code_sha, inputs} (sisteer.registry.analysis). |
| `name` | TEXT | NOT NULL |  | The analysis's name, dotted by study (`moe_routing.capture`); free text, unique only with the code sha and inputs. |
| `code_sha` | TEXT | NOT NULL | pattern `SHA1_OR_UNVERIFIED` | The commit the analysis ran from (forty hex), or 'unverified'. |
| `code_ref` | TEXT | nullable |  | a code sha alone names the code |
| `cluster_job_ids_json` | TEXT | NOT NULL default '[]' | pattern `JSON` | The scheduler job ids that produced it (strings), in the filer's order; [] for a local computation. |
| `substrate` | TEXT | NOT NULL | `SUBSTRATES` | Where it ran. |
| `report_uri` | TEXT | nullable |  | an analysis whose outputs are pages alone files no report |
| `report_sha256` | TEXT | nullable | pattern `SHA256` | paired with report_uri (the table CHECK): null exactly when no report is filed |
| `filed_utc` | TEXT | NOT NULL | pattern `UTC_MS` | When the filing was written (the filer's clock). |
| `filed_by` | TEXT | NOT NULL |  | Whose work the analysis is (by default); the relaying session is `extra_json.provenance.relayed_by`. |
| `notes` | TEXT | nullable |  | free text |
| `extra_json` | TEXT | NOT NULL default '{}' | pattern `JSON` | `provenance` {kind: user_direct|relayed, relayed_by, message_utc}, the spec's own `extra`, and any unknown record field. |
| `record_written_utc` | TEXT | NOT NULL | pattern `UTC_MS` | The written_utc of the filing whose header this row is: with record_sha256 the row's ordering key (the smallest among the id's filings is kept). |
| `record_sha256` | TEXT | NOT NULL | pattern `SHA256` | The record sha of the filing kept (see record_written_utc). |
| `record_uri` | TEXT | NOT NULL |  | The logical uri (`<file>#<line>`) of the filing kept, so a displaced filing can be refused by name. |

Table constraints: `analysis_report_pairing`. Indexes: `idx_analysis_filed` (filed_utc).

### `analysis_input` (ledger-scale)

One input an analysis read: an ingested run or an object. The input is named twice -- `input_id` in the key and the one FK column of its kind (`run_id` for a run, `object_id` for an object; the table CHECK pairs them) -- so the harvester's dependency check reads the parent through the declared FK (validate.parent_references) and the key stays one column wide. A ledger-fact kind cannot wait in `blocked_records`, so a row naming a run or object the registry does not hold is REFUSED by name, never queued (harvest.Ingestor.apply_validated); `registry analysis file` read-checks every input before it writes.

Primary key: (`analysis_id`, `input_kind`, `input_id`)

| column | type | null | check / reference | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `analysis_id` | TEXT | NOT NULL | → `analysis.analysis_id` |  |
| `filing_sha256` | TEXT | NOT NULL | pattern `SHA256` | The record sha of the `analysis` header (the filing) that wrote this row; the row folds only while that filing is the kept one or a duplicate of it. |
| `input_kind` | TEXT | NOT NULL | `ANALYSIS_INPUT_KINDS` |  |
| `input_id` | TEXT | NOT NULL |  | The run_id or object_id, as the kind says. |
| `run_id` | TEXT | nullable | → `run.run_id` | an object input names no run |
| `object_id` | TEXT | nullable | → `object.object_id` | a run input names no object |
| `extra_json` | TEXT | NOT NULL default '{}' | pattern `JSON` | What the analysis read of the input (`role`: the steering condition, the transcript set), as the filer wrote it. |
| `record_written_utc` | TEXT | NOT NULL | pattern `UTC_MS` | The written_utc of the record this row is: with record_sha256 the row's ordering key (the smallest among the key's records is kept). |
| `record_sha256` | TEXT | NOT NULL | pattern `SHA256` | The record sha of the record kept (see record_written_utc). |
| `record_uri` | TEXT | NOT NULL |  | The logical uri (`<file>#<line>`) of the record kept, so a displaced record can be refused by name. |

Table constraints: `analysis_input_kind_pairing`. Indexes: `idx_analysis_input_run` (run_id) where `run_id IS NOT NULL`, `idx_analysis_input_object` (object_id) where `object_id IS NOT NULL`.

### `analysis_artifact` (ledger-scale)

One registered file of an analysis: the link from the analysis to an `artifact` row -- its report, a file of a published page directory, a figure -- with the file's ROLE to the analysis. The artifact rows themselves are written by the same filing (through publish.register_files, kind by suffix; a remote report under its declared sha) ahead of this row, so the FK parent folds first.

Primary key: (`analysis_id`, `artifact_id`)

| column | type | null | check / reference | note |

| `artifact_id` | TEXT | NOT NULL | → `artifact.artifact_id` |  |
| `role` | TEXT | NOT NULL | `ANALYSIS_ARTIFACT_ROLES` |  |
| `extra_json` | TEXT | NOT NULL default '{}' | pattern `JSON` | `page_url` / `page_dir` for a file of a published page directory; `declared_sha256` for a remote report. |
| `record_written_utc` | TEXT | NOT NULL | pattern `UTC_MS` | The written_utc of the record this row is: with record_sha256 the row's ordering key (the smallest among the key's records is kept). |
| `record_sha256` | TEXT | NOT NULL | pattern `SHA256` | The record sha of the record kept (see record_written_utc). |
| `record_uri` | TEXT | NOT NULL |  | The logical uri (`<file>#<line>`) of the record kept, so a displaced record can be refused by name. |

Indexes: `idx_analysis_artifact_artifact` (artifact_id).

### `ordered_fact_record` (ledger-scale)

Every record of an ORDERED ledger-fact table (records.LEDGER_ORDERED_TABLES: the three analysis tables) the fold has applied, by the record's table and natural key -- the kept record, its duplicates, the records it displaced and the ones that conflict with it alike; one row per record sha. Written by `reducer.Reducer.apply_ledger_fact` on every outcome, so a rebuild carries the same rows; read by the harvester when the kept record of a key MOVES (an earlier-sorting record arrived late) to judge every other record of the key again against the new kept one (`harvest.Ingestor._rejudge_refilings`): a record identical to it is accepted (its conflict refusal withdrawn), one that differs is refused by name -- the one accepted as a duplicate of the displaced record included, which leaves no refusal row to find, so without this index live and rebuild would refuse different sets. Carriers only, never payloads: a record is judged again from its immutable file. Not `row_history` (a ledger fact has no fold events).

Primary key: (`table_name`, `natural_key_json`, `record_sha256`)

| column | type | null | check / reference | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `table_name` | TEXT | NOT NULL |  | The ordered table (a key of records.LEDGER_ORDERED_TABLES); no CHECK list, so a table ordered later adds rows and the shape stands. |
| `natural_key_json` | TEXT | NOT NULL | pattern `JSON` | Canonical JSON of the record's natural-key columns, as `row_history` keys a run-scale row. |
| `record_sha256` | TEXT | NOT NULL | pattern `SHA256` | The record (records.record_sha). |
| `record_type` | TEXT | NOT NULL |  | The record's kind (the refusal row of a record judged again names it). |
| `record_uri` | TEXT | NOT NULL |  | The record's logical uri (`<file>#<line>`); the smallest when the same record arrives under two names. |
| `written_utc` | TEXT | NOT NULL | pattern `UTC_MS` | The record's written_utc: with record_sha256 its place in the key's order. |

### `ordered_fact_carrier` (ledger-scale)

Every ARRIVAL of a record of an ordered ledger-fact table (records.LEDGER_ORDERED_TABLES), whatever its verdict: the logical uri that carried it and the side of that file's delivery audit (`record_delivery`) the record is counted on -- `accepted` (the file's `n_ok` or `n_duplicate`) or `refused` (its `n_refused`). One row per (record, uri): the same record copied to a second uri has two rows where `ordered_fact_record` keeps one carrier. Written by `harvest.Ingestor.apply_validated` as the fold counts the record for its file; read and moved by `harvest.Ingestor._move_record_delivery` when the record is judged again after its file's fold (a filing displaced, a re-filing or a child judged again, a dependency refusal accepted on retry), so EVERY file that carried the record follows the verdict -- a mover that followed `ordered_fact_record`'s one canonical carrier alone would leave a filing's copy under a second uri at `ok` after the filing was displaced, and the status page would list it as ingested. A pure function of the records once the moves are made (a record's standing verdict, per file that carried it), so a rebuild writes the same rows and the table is compared by `harvest.verify_equal`; the `ok` / `duplicate` split it does not record is the fold's arrival order, the reason `record_delivery` itself is not compared.

Primary key: (`table_name`, `record_sha256`, `record_uri`)

| column | type | null | check / reference | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `table_name` | TEXT | NOT NULL |  | The ordered table (a key of records.LEDGER_ORDERED_TABLES); no CHECK list, as `ordered_fact_record`. |
| `record_sha256` | TEXT | NOT NULL | pattern `SHA256` | The record (records.record_sha). |
| `record_uri` | TEXT | NOT NULL |  | The logical uri (`<file>#<line>`) this arrival of the record came under; the file before `#` is the delivery row's. |
| `delivery` | TEXT | NOT NULL | `DELIVERY_SIDES` | The side of the file's delivery audit the record is counted on: `accepted` (`n_ok` or `n_duplicate`) or `refused` (`n_refused`); moved with the file's counts when the record is judged again. |

### `fold_observation` (ledger-scale)

The harvester's OBSERVATIONS about a record at the fold, none of them a refusal: a detector over the fold's own output, never a fold rule -- the record folded exactly as it always does (replace-at-key is universal). One row per (kind, run, restating record). Derived by `reducer.Reducer.apply_run_scale` from the run key's ordered events and fold snapshots after every refold of the key (the key's rows replaced whole, so a late-arriving earlier-stamped record re-derives them as it re-derives `row_history.folded_state_json`), and once by the migration that created the table for the runs already folded. A pure function of the log: a rebuild carries the same rows, no column excluded; the cycle that folded the restating record is its file's arrival (`record_ingest`), joined at read time by `registry observations`. Not the `observation` table (a source revision's membership of a run-scale key).

Primary key: (`observation_kind`, `run_id`, `record_sha256`)

| column | type | null | check / reference | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `observation_kind` | TEXT | NOT NULL | `FOLD_OBSERVATION_KINDS` | What was observed (vocab.FOLD_OBSERVATION_KINDS). |
| `run_id` | TEXT | NOT NULL | → `run.run_id` | The run whose folded state the record restated. |
| `record_sha256` | TEXT | NOT NULL | pattern `SHA256` | The RESTATING record (records.record_sha): the `run` or `run_patch` event that carried the smaller set. |
| `record_type` | TEXT | NOT NULL |  | The restating record's kind: `run` (a re-registration) or `run_patch`. |
| `record_uri` | TEXT | NOT NULL |  | The record file (logical path) that carried the restating record -- the event's carrier in `row_history`, following the canonical carrier when the same record arrives under two names. |
| `written_utc` | TEXT | NOT NULL | pattern `UTC_MS` | The restating record's written_utc: its position in the fold's order (never the cycle that folded it). |
| `folded_record_sha256` | TEXT | NOT NULL | pattern `SHA256` | The record whose statement the folded set came from: the latest earlier event of the key that stated `extra.serving_jobs`. |
| `folded_json` | TEXT | NOT NULL | pattern `JSON` | The set the run's extra_json held before the restatement, as a sorted JSON array of its members. |
| `restated_json` | TEXT | NOT NULL | pattern `JSON` | The set the record stated, as a sorted JSON array of its distinct members (order and duplicates in the record are not facts). |
| `dropped_json` | TEXT | NOT NULL | pattern `JSON` | The members of the folded set the restatement left out, sorted. |
| `n_dropped` | INTEGER | NOT NULL | pattern `NONNEG` | len(dropped_json): the rank for `registry observations summary`. |

Indexes: `idx_fold_observation_written` (written_utc).
